Sets process.exitCode to 1 if none of the specified identifiers are found in the source file.\n\n```ts\nimport * as ts from \"typescript\";\n\n/**\n * Prints out particular nodes from a source file\n * \n * @param file a path to a file\n * @param identifiers top level identifiers available\n */\nfunction extract(file: string, identifiers: string[]): void {\n  // Create a Program to represent the project, then pull out the\n  // source file to parse its AST.\n  let program = ts.createProgram([file], { allowJs: true });\n  const sourceFile = program.getSourceFile(file);\n  \n  // To print the AST, we'll use TypeScript's printer\n  const printer = ts.createPrinter({ newLine: ts.NewLineKind.LineFeed });\n\n  // To give constructive error messages, keep track of found and un-found identifiers\n  const unfoundNodes = [], foundNodes = [];\n\n  // Loop through the root AST nodes of the file\n  ts.forEachChild(sourceFile, node => {\n    let name = \"\";\n    \n    // This is an incomplete set of AST nodes which could have a top level identifier\n    // it's left to you to expand this list, which you can do by using\n    // https://ts-ast-viewer.com/ to see the AST of a file then use the same patterns\n    // as below\n    if (ts.isFunctionDeclaration(node)) {\n      name = node.name.text;\n      // Hide the method body when printing\n      node.body = undefined;\n    } else if (ts.isVariableStatement(node)) {\n      name = node.declarationList.declarations[0].name.getText(sourceFile);\n    } else if (ts.isInterfaceDeclaration(node)){\n      name = node.name.text\n    }\n\n    const container = identifiers.includes(name) ? foundNodes : unfoundNodes;\n    container.push([name, node]);\n  });\n\n  // Either print the found nodes, or offer a list of what identifiers were found\n  if (!foundNodes.length) {\n    console.log(`Could not find any of ${identifiers.join(\", \")} in ${file}, found: ${unfoundNodes.filter(f => f[0]).map(f => f[0]).join(\", \")}.`);\n    process.exitCode = 1;\n  } else {\n    foundNodes.map(f => {\n      const [name, node] = f;\n      console.log(\"### \" + name + \"\\n\");\n      console.log(printer.printNode(ts.EmitHint.Unspecified, node, sourceFile)) + \"\\n\";\n    });\n  }\n}\n\n// Run the extract function with the script's arguments\nextract(process.argv[2], process.argv.slice(3));\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### SourceFile.imports — alternative for parsing imports\n\nSource: https://github.com/microsoft/typescript/blob/main/packages/typescript/src/ast/ast.ts\n\nSince there is no local parser in the client library, import declarations are parsed server-side. The returned `SourceFile` exposes an `imports` property containing the parsed `ImportDeclaration` nodes, providing the alternative path for inspecting imports.\n\n```typescript\n    readonly imports: readonly Node[];\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### createSourceFile entry point\n\nSource: https://github.com/microsoft/typescript/blob/main/tsc/testdata/fixtures/compiler/parser.ts\n\nParses source text into a SourceFile AST.
